mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer demand and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 50,000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during these episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% and 10% quarter-over-quarter, respectively, signals a demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ change > 2% AND HOUST QoQ change > 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies exceed these thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between industrial production (INDPRO) and S&P 500 returns exists: monthly increases in INDPRO of more than 0.3% are associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting improved supply and earnings expectations.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 0.3% monthly change is not followed by a positive S&P 500 5-day return in more than 60% of cases over the next five years.
